From 0a30288da1aec914e158c2d7a3482a85f632750f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2014 15:24:32 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] blk-mq, percpu_ref: implement a kludge for SCSI blk-mq stall
 during probe

blk-mq uses percpu_ref for its usage counter which tracks the number
of in-flight commands and used to synchronously drain the queue on
freeze.  percpu_ref shutdown takes measureable wallclock time as it
involves a sched RCU grace period.  This means that draining a blk-mq
takes measureable wallclock time.  One would think that this shouldn't
matter as queue shutdown should be a rare event which takes place
asynchronously w.r.t. userland.

Unfortunately, SCSI probing involves synchronously setting up and then
tearing down a lot of request_queues back-to-back for non-existent
LUNs.  This means that SCSI probing may take more than ten seconds
when scsi-mq is used.

This will be properly fixed by implementing a mechanism to keep
q->mq_usage_counter in atomic mode till genhd registration; however,
that involves rather big updates to percpu_ref which is difficult to
apply late in the devel cycle (v3.17-rc6 at the moment).  As a
stop-gap measure till the proper fix can be implemented in the next
cycle, this patch introduces __percpu_ref_kill_expedited() and makes
blk_mq_freeze_queue() use it.  This is heavy-handed but should work
for testing the experimental SCSI blk-mq implementation.

Signed-off-by: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>
Reported-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@infradead.org>
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/g/20140919113815.GA10791@lst.de
Fixes: add703fda981 ("blk-mq: use percpu_ref for mq usage count")
Cc: Kent Overstreet <kmo@daterainc.com>
Cc: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
Tested-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@fb.com>

diff --git a/include/linux/percpu-refcount.h b/include/linux/percpu-refcount.h
index 3dfbf237cd8f..ef5894ca8e50 100644
--- a/include/linux/percpu-refcount.h
+++ b/include/linux/percpu-refcount.h
@@ -71,6 +71,7 @@ void percpu_ref_reinit(struct percpu_ref *ref);
 void percpu_ref_exit(struct percpu_ref *ref);
 void percpu_ref_kill_and_confirm(struct percpu_ref *ref,
 				 percpu_ref_func_t *confirm_kill);
+void __percpu_ref_kill_expedited(struct percpu_ref *ref);
 
 /**
  * percpu_ref_kill - drop the initial ref

diff --git a/block/blk-mq.c b/block/blk-mq.c
index c88e6089746d..df8e1e09dd17 100644
--- a/block/blk-mq.c
+++ b/block/blk-mq.c
@@ -119,7 +119,16 @@ void blk_mq_freeze_queue(struct request_queue *q)
 	spin_unlock_irq(q->queue_lock);
 
 	if (freeze) {
-		percpu_ref_kill(&q->mq_usage_counter);
+		/*
+		 * XXX: Temporary kludge to work around SCSI blk-mq stall.
+		 * SCSI synchronously creates and destroys many queues
+		 * back-to-back during probe leading to lengthy stalls.
+		 * This will be fixed by keeping ->mq_usage_counter in
+		 * atomic mode until genhd registration, but, for now,
+		 * let's work around using expedited synchronization.
+		 */
+		__percpu_ref_kill_expedited(&q->mq_usage_counter);
+
 		blk_mq_run_queues(q, false);
 	}
 	wait_event(q->mq_freeze_wq, percpu_ref_is_zero(&q->mq_usage_counter));

diff --git a/lib/percpu-refcount.c b/lib/percpu-refcount.c
index fe5a3342e960..a89cf09a8268 100644
--- a/lib/percpu-refcount.c
+++ b/lib/percpu-refcount.c
@@ -184,3 +184,19 @@ void percpu_ref_kill_and_confirm(struct percpu_ref *ref,
 	call_rcu_sched(&ref->rcu, percpu_ref_kill_rcu);
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(percpu_ref_kill_and_confirm);
+
+/*
+ * XXX: Temporary kludge to work around SCSI blk-mq stall.  Used only by
+ * block/blk-mq.c::blk_mq_freeze_queue().  Will be removed during v3.18
+ * devel cycle.  Do not use anywhere else.
+ */
+void __percpu_ref_kill_expedited(struct percpu_ref *ref)
+{
+	WARN_ONCE(ref->pcpu_count_ptr & PCPU_REF_DEAD,
+		  "percpu_ref_kill() called more than once on %pf!",
+		  ref->release);
+
+	ref->pcpu_count_ptr |= PCPU_REF_DEAD;
+	synchronize_sched_expedited();
+	percpu_ref_kill_rcu(&ref->rcu);
+}
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **`include/linux/percpu-refcount.h`**
   - Added a new function declaration: `void __percpu_ref_kill_expedited(struct percpu_ref *ref);`

2. **`block/blk-mq.c`**
   - Modified the `blk_mq_freeze_queue` function:
     - Replaced the call to `percpu_ref_kill(&q->mq_usage_counter);` with `__percpu_ref_kill_expedited(&q->mq_usage_counter);`.
     - Added comments explaining the reason for this change, highlighting it as a temporary kludge to address SCSI blk-mq stalls during probing.

3. **`lib/percpu-refcount.c`**
   - Implemented the `__percpu_ref_kill_expedited` function:
     - This function marks the reference as dead and synchronizes the scheduler in an expedited manner.
     - It includes a warning if the function is called more than once on the same reference.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications across the three files are interconnected as follows:

- The new function `__percpu_ref_kill_expedited` is introduced in `percpu-refcount.h` and implemented in `percpu-refcount.c` to provide a faster way to handle the shutdown of the `percpu_ref` reference counter.
- In `blk-mq.c`, the existing method for freezing the queue (`percpu_ref_kill`) is replaced with this new expedited method to mitigate the performance issues caused by SCSI probing, which involves rapid creation and destruction of request queues.
- The comments added in `blk-mq.c` clarify that this change is a temporary workaround until a more robust solution can be implemented in future development cycles. This indicates a planned evolution of the codebase, where the new function serves a specific purpose in the context of addressing an immediate performance concern.

   - Introduced a new function `__percpu_ref_kill_expedited(struct percpu_ref *ref)`. This function is designed as a temporary workaround for the SCSI blk-mq stall issue. It marks the reference as dead and performs expedited synchronization to handle the shutdown of the percpu_ref.

- The addition of the function declaration in `percpu-refcount.h` ensures that the new functionality is properly integrated into the existing codebase, allowing other components to reference it as needed. 

Overall, these changes are part of a stop-gap measure to enhance the performance of the SCSI blk-mq subsystem until a more comprehensive solution can be implemented in future development cycles.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
percpu_ref_kill(&q->mq_usage_counter);
wait_event(q->mq_freeze_wq, percpu_ref_is_zero(&q->mq_usage_counter));
```
Reason:
The `percpu_ref_kill()` function initiates a shutdown of the `mq_usage_counter`, which involves a scheduling RCU grace period, causing significant delays. This is problematic during SCSI probing, where multiple request queues are set up and torn down synchronously, leading to extended stalls in the block-mq when handling non-existent LUNs.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
__percpu_ref_kill_expedited(&q->mq_usage_counter);
```
Reason:
The `__percpu_ref_kill_expedited()` function provides a more immediate and expedited way to handle the shutdown of the `mq_usage_counter`, reducing the wallclock time associated with the RCU grace period.
